item.title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
item.description: arXiv:2611.08591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $\Delta(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+\epsilon)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Behtash, Syo Kamata, Mauricio M. Martinez

item.title: Standard Subspaces and Modular Theory -- General Theory and Applications to QFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.08668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a preview of an upcoming monograph on standard subspaces and modular theory. At the moment, it consists of the first chapter. This starts with a gentle introduction to the subject, and then describes the modular theory of standard subspaces, the characterization of their modular data by the KMS condition and reflection positivity, and various constructions of standard subspaces. Further topics in Chapter 1 include the connection of standard subspaces to complexifications and symplectic structures, including their polarizers, and operations with standard subspaces, namely direct sums, direct integrals, and tensor products. Many examples and classification results are included as well. This first chapter also contains a description of the free U(1)-current and some other applications to quantum field theory, such as KMS states of type I factors, the local subspaces of the free Klein--Gordon field, and the entropy operator defined by a standard subspace.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Correa da Silva, Gandalf Lechner, Roberto Longo

item.title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.
item.dc:creator: G. Ortenzi, G. Roberti, M. Sommacal

item.title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.
item.dc:creator: Erik Brodsky, Leonid O Chekhov, Quanyu Tang

item.title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.09034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $\mu \to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.
item.dc:creator: Lei Liu, Pedro A. S. Salom\~ao

item.title: Zak Phase, Pole--Zero Invariants and the Maslov Index of Bloch Cauchy Lines in One-Dimensional Periodic Media
item.description: arXiv:2611.09419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The topological properties of the Bloch bands of a one-dimensional periodic medium are described either by the Berry--Zak phase or by the poles and zeros of the surface impedance. We show that both can be read from one geometric object: the line spanned by the field and its flux (the Cauchy data) at an inversion centre. For each band, this line turns as the quasi-momentum runs over the Brillouin zone. Its number of turns, the Maslov index, is fixed by the parities (even or odd) of the Bloch functions at the two band edges, and its parity is the Zak phase. In a gap, the Cauchy line of the solution decaying on one side rotates monotonically with the energy, and an interface state between two crystals is a crossing of two such lines. This gives the known criterion of at most one state per gap in terms of the same lines. Examples with a stratified medium show that the choice of inversion centre changes the interface spectrum. The last section discusses what is missing to extend the construction to higher dimension.
item.dc:creator: Didier Felbacq

item.title: Radiation principle for discrete acoustic equation on graphs with several cylindrical outlets to infinity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A discrete analogue of the acoustic equation with a spectral parameter is studied on graphs with several cylindrical outlets to infinity. At infinity in each cylindrical outlet the coefficients of this equation converge exponentially fast to periodic functions. It is assumed that the spectral parameter is fixed and distinct from thresholds and flat bands. We construct a special basis of the continuous spectrum eigenfunctions (bounded solutions of the homogeneous equation that do not belong to l2), introduce the scattering matrix, and establish the radiation principle (a well-posed statement of the problem with radiation conditions at infinity).
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Poretskii, Danil Smorchkov

item.title: Absence of Excited Bound States for All Fibers of the Fr\"ohlich Polaron at Weak Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.09586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the discrete spectrum of the three-dimensional Fr\"ohlich polaron at weak coupling and fixed total momentum. We prove that, for sufficiently small coupling and every total momentum $0<|\xi|\le 1/4$, the ground-state eigenvalue is the only eigenvalue below the essential spectrum. Our proof builds on the analogous zero-momentum result of Seiringer (2023). Combined with that result and the work of Dahlbaek (2017), this implies that, at sufficiently weak coupling, no fiber Hamiltonian has a discrete excited eigenvalue.
item.dc:creator: David Mitrouskas

item.title: Finite-strain second-gradient elasticity with an energetic surface: existence of minimizers, incremental theory and elastocapillary beading
item.description: arXiv:2611.09587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite-strain theory of second-gradient elasticity for solids with a material surface endowed with its own constitutive energy. The bulk second gradient plays two complementary roles. First, under suitable coercivity assumptions and convexity with respect to the second gradient, we prove the existence of minimizers for nonnegative, lower semicontinuous surface energy densities, without requiring convexity, polyconvexity, positive one-homogeneity, or an upper growth bound on the surface energy. Second, it introduces an intrinsic bulk length scale that affects the onset of instability and wavelength selection. To investigate these effects, we derive an incremental small-on-large formulation in the finitely deformed configuration and apply it to the elastocapillary beading of an axially stretched soft cylinder. For an infinite cylinder and the parameters considered, increasing the second-gradient modulus delays bifurcation and shifts the critical mode towards longer wavelengths. Above a finite threshold of this modulus, the critical stretch saturates in the long-wave limit. The model is implemented in the open-source finite element code OOFEM using C1-continuous isogeometric analysis. Finite-cylinder simulations yield onset stretches in close agreement with the analytical predictions. Selected post-bifurcation branches traced by arc-length continuation exhibit beaded states and supercritical bifurcation at small second-gradient moduli, whereas larger moduli are associated with subcritical bifurcation and the formation of distinct thick and thin segments.
item.dc:creator: Michal \v{S}mejkal, Martin Hor\'ak, Martin Kru\v{z}\'ik

item.title: A scalable computational framework for PDEs on physical networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.09833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transport, reaction and wave propagation on physical networks depend on dynamics along edges and interactions at junctions. We present a flexible framework for modeling physical networks at scale. A network calculus expresses edge dynamics and vertex contributions as fields over the whole network. Differential operators satisfy integration by parts-identities that connect local dynamics to global conservation laws, and explicit vertex constraints allow a variety of physical junction conditions. We implement this formalism using the open-source Dedalus spectral framework. This accommodates heterogeneous edge lengths, material properties and spectral resolutions. Initial-value, boundary-value and eigenvalue problems share a parallel solution method that eliminates internal unknowns independently on subgraphs and couples their solutions through shared boundary vertex interfaces. We verify numerical convergence and demonstrate strong and weak scaling on networks with millions of edges. We present applications to localized optical resonances in photonic networks, preferential channel formation during mineral replacement in evolving pore networks, and nonlinear dispersive waves for KdV on a periodic network.
item.dc:creator: Sidney Holden, Keaton J. Burns, Daniel Lecoanet, Jeffrey S. Oishi, Benjamin P. Brown, Geoffrey M. Vasil

item.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-filled $3$-manifolds along fundamental shadow link complements with big volume
item.description: arXiv:2611.08517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Volume Conjecture and the Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for closed oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn-fillings along a fundamental shadow link complement, provided that their volumes are sufficiently close to that of the complement. More generally, we show that the conjectured asymptotic expansions hold for pairs obtained by change-of-pair operations on a fundamental shadow link complement whenever the volume of the corresponding hyperbolic cone manifold is sufficiently close to that of the complement. A key ingredient in the proof is the introduction of extended quantum $6j$-symbols and a Weak Reflection Symmetry satisfied by them. The Weak Reflection Symmetry is established by relating the extended quantum $6j$-symbols to the $b$-$6j$ symbols through a real Gevrey-$1$ estimate and a truncated Borel-Laplace transform.
item.dc:creator: Yunpeng Meng, Baojun Wu, Tian Yang, Yuxuan Yang

item.title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.08609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.
item.dc:creator: Jingbo Wan, Yipeng Wang

item.title: Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.08661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Rudi Weikard

item.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.08958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Matheus G. Barbosa

item.title: Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
item.description: arXiv:2611.09018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.
item.dc:creator: Davide Batic, Denys Dutykh

item.title: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
item.description: arXiv:2611.09032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from infrared divergences
item.dc:creator: Albert Schwarz

item.title: Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification
item.description: arXiv:2611.09137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.
item.dc:creator: Zetao Fei, Josselin Garnier

item.title: Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.09151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.
item.dc:creator: Federico Camia, Jianping Jiang, Charles M. Newman

item.title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schr\"odinger operators with complex potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.09301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schr\"odinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $\alpha>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: B. Shapiro

item.title: Natural potentials for TT tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data
item.description: arXiv:2611.09303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $N$ be a natural tensor which vanishes at a metric $g\_0$. By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Erwann Delay (LMA, AU)

item.title: A Geometric Journey Through the Aharonov--Bohm Effect: Tonomura's Toroid, Pseudoscalar Phase, and Quantum Holonomy in Clifford Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.09311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The magnetic Aharonov--Bohm (AB) effect is often introduced through the idealised infinite solenoid and a complex scalar phase. We give a geometric-algebra formulation based on the compact toroidal magnets shielded by a superconductor employed in the electron-holography experiments of Tonomura and collaborators. Working in the real Euclidean Clifford algebra $ \mathrm{Cl}(3,0)$, we distinguish the unit volume pseudoscalar $I$ (grade 3), coordinate angles (scalars, grade 0), tangent vectors (grade 1), and directed surface bivectors (grade 2). The magnetic field is represented by the dual bivector $\mathcal{B}= I \mathbf B$, while the electromagnetic $U(1)$ phase is represented by the central unit multivector $e^{I\alpha}$ generated by the pseudoscalar $I$, rather than by a spatial rotor with a bivector generator. We establish the linked toroidal geometry, formulate magnetic flux and Stokes' theorem intrinsically in geometric algebra, and derive the holonomy element $U_\Gamma=\exp(Iq\Phi_B/\hbar)$ from $U(1)$ gauge covariance, with every sign fixed explicitly. We then express superconducting fluxoid quantization in the same notation and obtain the binary electron holonomy $U_\Gamma = (-1)^N$ in the ideal limit where the linked magnetic flux equals $N h/(2e)$. Finally, a short conditional-state description of the quantum source and field shows how a backreaction can introduce an additional phase and reduce interference visibility. The conditional-state overlap is represented by a central scalar--pseudoscalar element; preservation of the fluxoid sector alone does not guarantee unit coherence.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Powell

item.title: Non-asymptotic First- and Second-Order Tail Brackets for the Kostlan-Shub-Smale Field and Spherical k-Spin Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the Kostlan-Shub-Smale field $X$ of degree $k\ge3$ on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we prove the two-sided bound $(1-\varepsilon(u))\,\delta_{*}(u)\le\mathbb{P}\{\sup X>u\}\le\delta_{*}(u)$ at every finite $(k,d)$, where $\delta_{*}(u)$ is the expected number of critical points above $u$, halved when $k$ is even, and $\varepsilon(u)$ is explicit for $\rho u\ge\min\{d-1,\frac32\sqrt{2(d-1)}\}$. The gap is therefore at most of order $e^{-(1+\rho^{2})u^{2}/2}$ with $\rho^{2}=k/(2(k-1))$. We also give $\delta_{*}$ itself in closed form, as a finite sum of Hermite polynomials, together with a two-term envelope that is asymptotically sharp and a single-monomial relaxation of the form $Cu^{d-2}e^{-u^{2}/2}$. As an application we bracket the annealed complexity of the spherical $k$-spin Hamiltonian at every finite $(k,d)$: the upper bound holds at every energy, a lower bound of the same form at every energy above $9/4$ times the spectral edge $\sqrt{2(d-1)}/\rho$, above twice the edge when $d\ge10$, and is consistent with the Auffinger-Ben Arous-\v{C}ern\'y complexity function as $d\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marc Aza\"is, Federico Dalmao, Yohann De Castro

item.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo

item.title: Singular Vortex in the Large Deviation of Empirical Current for Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process
item.description: arXiv:2611.09526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a large deviation estimate for singular current observables of the two-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process. In particular, the observable has a non-standard large deviation scaling $N^2(\log N)^{-1}$ due to the presence of singular vortices, whereby trajectories rotating near the origin point yield an enhanced contribution to the current observable. The proof combines the heuristics of Bodineau-Derrida-Lebowitz 2008, the averaging method of Jara-Menezes 2018, and novel cancellation and multi-scale renormalization arguments developed by this paper.
item.dc:creator: Chenjiayue Qi

item.title: Mode interaction in inclined-layer convection: a physical interpretation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We carry out a numerical investigation of the Oberbeck--Boussinesq equations in a fluid layer inclined against gravity. Equilibria containing different numbers of co-rotating rolls are computed. Mixed-mode branches connect branches containing states with four and six identical co-rotating rolls. These branches display two contrasting routes to reducing (or increasing) the number of rolls, one in which rolls disappear (or appear) and another route in which rolls merge (or split). These results are interpreted in light of the $(2,3)$ mode interaction scenario.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Zheng, Laurette S. Tuckerman, Tobias M. Schneider

item.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.09630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.
item.dc:creator: Ohad Silbiger, Yakir Hadad

item.title: Remark on residual solutions in the $KBc$ algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.09761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study residual solutions of open bosonic string field theory in the $KBc$ algebra with the auxiliary identities $(\partial^mc)^2=0$ of the ghost field. These solutions are not covered by the classification based on the defining relations alone. We show that the operator which controls the cohomology on the residual family depends only on $s=\gamma_1+\gamma_2$. At positive level $n$, cohomology can appear only on the lines $s=\pm n$. We compute it through level four and find one class at every point of each line $s=-3$ and $s=-4$. These classes give exact polynomial deformations of the residual family. At level six on $s=-6$, the cohomology instead vanishes generically and has dimension two at $(-1,-5)$ and $(-5,-1)$. We also compute the failure of the standard generator redefinition to preserve the auxiliary identities, and discuss the regularization of an explicit residual solution.
item.dc:creator: Ilmar Gahramanov

item.title: The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume
item.description: arXiv:2611.09776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the one-dimensional block Anderson model with independent $W\times W$ Gaussian unitary ensemble potentials and deterministic nearest-neighbor hopping, with hopping-to-disorder ratio $g$. The system consists of $L$ blocks, with total dimension $N=WL$. As $W\to\infty$, we identify the bulk localization length, up to an arbitrarily small power of $W$, with $\min\{N,\max\{W,W^2g^2\}\}$, uniformly for deterministic couplings $g\ge0$ and cycle lengths $L\ge3$. For every fixed $D>0$ and all sufficiently large $W$, the expected fraction of eigenvectors in the selected energy interval satisfying these bounds is at least $1-W^{-D}$. In polynomial volume the bounds hold simultaneously for all eigenvectors in that interval with probability at least $1-W^{-D}$. The localization length is the number of coordinates in the shortest cyclic interval containing at least half of an eigenvector's mass.
item.dc:creator: Jun Yin

item.title: On Superconformal Index Degenerations and Half-Indices in S-Confining Gauge Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.09820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the $p \rightarrow 0$ limit of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal indices and its relation to half-indices of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories. At the level of special functions, this limit reduces elliptic hypergeometric integrals to basic hypergeometric integrals. The scaling of the flavor fugacities determines the Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions of the chiral multiplets. The gauge multiplet has Neumann boundary conditions. We apply this prescription to s-confining theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$, $USp(2N)$, $G_2$, and $SU(N)$, and recover the half-index identities of several boundary confining dualities, expressed through the Nassrallah-Rahman and Gustafson integrals. For $SU(N)$ with a rank-two antisymmetric chiral, four fundamentals and $N$ antifundamentals, we obtain an analytic proof of the half-index identities proposed by Okazaki and Smith for all $N \geq 5$.
item.dc:creator: Melisa Do\u{g}an, Ilmar Gahramanov

item.title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
item.description: arXiv:2611.09837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$. We show that this operator agrees with the Hamiltonian on the ground-state subspace and has a spectral gap. For SU(2) specifically, the representation theory of the singlet sector gives an astronomical reduction in the number of degrees of freedom. This allows us to construct an efficient variational basis whose inner products we compute exactly. We demonstrate the method by computing a state that satisfies rigorous bounds on its energy $E\,g_{\mathrm{YM}}^{-2/3}\leq 4.18\times10^{-8}$ and ground-subspace overlap $\|P_{\ker H}\psi\|^2\geq 0.999997$. We compute ground-state moments with high precision, finding values consistent with the bounds from our matrix bootstrap. Additionally, the state accurately reproduces both the exponent and coefficient of the asymptotic radial probability density predicted by the three-graviton amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Michel, Jaroslav Scheinpflug, Xi Yin

item.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.09861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schr\"odinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.
item.dc:creator: Ghansham Chandel, Siddhartha Das

item.title: Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
item.description: arXiv:2611.09867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. While they have fundamental theoretical implications, their existence has not been rigorously established. This is particularly subtle in the setting of the full infinite-dimensional bootstrap, i.e. the limit of zero numerical truncation. In this article, we prove that extremal solutions exist for OPE maximisation problems in 1d CFT. These are a large class of generically interacting, unitary, exact solutions of the crossing equation that maximise an OPE coefficient. We also prove that these problems have 'zero duality gap', meaning there exist functionals arbitrarily close to extremality. Our approach is to formulate the bootstrap as a convex optimisation problem in a Hilbert space and apply the Fenchel-Rockafellar theorem.
item.dc:creator: Filip Her\v{c}ek, Nat Levine

item.title: Twice Fourier transformable measures and diffraction theory
item.description: arXiv:2411.14987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mathematical diffraction theory has been developed since about 1995. Hof's initial approach relied on tempered distributions in euclidean space. Nowadays often the Fourier theory by Argabright and Gil de Lamadrid is used, which applies to appropriate measures on locally compact abelian groups. We review diffraction theory using Wiener amalgams as test function spaces. For translation bounded measures, this unifies and simplifies the former two approaches. We treat weighted versions of Meyer's model sets as examples.
item.dc:creator: Hans G. Feichtinger, Christoph Richard, Christoph Schumacher, Nicolae Strungaru

item.title: A Note on the Resolvent Algebra and Functional Integral Approach to the Free Bose Einstein Condensation
item.description: arXiv:2604.01424v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quasiparticles whose number is not conserved are generally considered not to condense in equilibrium, although a Bose--Einstein condensation can formally appear in particle--Bose field interacting systems. As a basis for examining this mathematically, we formulate the condensation of the free Bose gas with resolvent algebras and probability theory: above the critical density, the condensate state is a standard complex Gaussian mixture of disjoint factor states, which is its central decomposition and corresponds to the ergodic decomposition of a Gaussian measure for the real-time evolution.
item.dc:creator: Yoshitsugu Sekine

item.title: Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.23772v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Shevyakov

item.title: Asymptotic quasi--local structure induced by Magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2609.26987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a magnetic coherent--state frame over the Landau levels of the two--dimensional Landau Hamiltonian, indexed by a discrete metric space combining spatial and energy degrees of freedom. Although overcomplete, the frame is almost--orthogonal, and we use it to endow the CAR $C^*$--algebra over the one--particle Hilbert space with an \emph{asymptotic quasi--local} (AQL) structure, in which graded commutators of observables localized on disjoint index sets decay exponentially rather than vanish exactly. By means of a family of conditional expectations onto the resulting local subalgebras, we construct a Fr\'echet $*$--subalgebra of almost--local observables, invariant under the discrete group of lattice translations, which act on it by continuous automorphisms. For the full continuous group of magnetic translations we establish a quantitative control on how local observables spread through this almost--local algebra, and we show that this control suffices to extend graded asymptotic abelianness from the lattice to the entire continuous translation group. The results provide a discrete--continuum dictionary intended as the starting point for extending Lieb--Robinson--type techniques from lattice systems to interacting continuum electrons in a magnetic field.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe De Nittis

item.title: Generalized Frobenius Structures on Hurwitz Spaces, Their Open Extensions and Associated Principal Hierarchies
item.description: arXiv:2610.39411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct generalized Frobenius structures on Hurwitz spaces of arbitrary genus using extended primary differentials. Through contour integrals involving the Cauchy kernel, we derive explicit dispersionless Lax representations for the principal hierarchies of these structures and their almost-dual counterparts. We also construct solutions to the open WDVV equations for both the original and almost-dual structures, and derive explicit principal hierarchies for the resulting rank-one extensions. Finally, we show that these constructions admit Shramchenko deformations.
item.dc:creator: Shilin Ma

item.title: A uniform trigonometric R-matrix for the exceptional series
item.description: arXiv:2406.01348v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The exceptional series is a finite list of points on a projective line with a simple Lie algebra attached to each point. This list of Lie algebras includes the five exceptional Lie algebras. We give a uniform trigonometric $R$-matrix for the exceptional series in the representation $L\oplus I$, where $L$ is the quantum deformation of the adjoint representation and $I$ is the trivial representation. We construct a sixteen dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit2)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^2(L\oplus I))$ and a 287 dimensional algebra, $A^\square(\mathit3)$, which interpolates the algebras $\mathrm{End}(\otimes^3(L\oplus I))$. The $R$-matrix lives in $A^\square(\mathit2)$ and satisfies the Yang-Baxter equation in $A^\square(\mathit3)$; it interpolates the trigonometric $R$-matrices for the points in the exceptional series.
item.dc:creator: Bruce W. Westbury, Paul Zinn-Justin

item.title: Phase diagram for intermittent maps
item.description: arXiv:2504.07864v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies the phase diagram of a fixed Pomeau--Manneville, or intermittent, map under a varying H\"older continuous potential of fixed exponent. Depending on the exponent, there are either one or two thermodynamic phases. The \emph{intermittent} phase is characterized by a unique Gibbs state whose typical orbits alternate irregularly between time intervals spent near the neutral fixed point and chaotic excursions away from it. The stationary phase is characterized by the Dirac mass at the neutral fixed point being the unique Gibbs state. Above a threshold exponent, every potential belongs to the intermittent phase, so the phase diagram is trivial. At or below the threshold, the phase transition locus is a co-dimension 1 topological submanifold separating the two phases, and it coincides with the set of potentials at which the pressure function fails to be real-analytic. This paper also investigates the relationships between the phase transition locus, (persistent) phase transitions in temperature, and ground states. It highlights a connection between phase transitions in temperature and ergodic optimization.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Coronel, Juan Rivera-Letelier

item.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
item.description: arXiv:2601.03209v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain's proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is for example $1,2^{1/3},2^{-1/3}$. This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature $(2,2)$. The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature $(3,3)$ in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})^3\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^3$ over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner's measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.
item.dc:creator: Wooyeon Kim, Jens Marklof, Matthew Welsh

item.title: On deforming and breaking integrability
item.description: arXiv:2603.17018v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we study nearest-neighbour deformations of integrable models. After expanding in the deformation parameter, we identify four possible types of deformations. First there are deformations that simply break or preserve integrability. Then we find two different subtle cases. The first case is where the deformation is only integrable if all orders of the deformation parameter are taken into account. An example of these are the long-range deformations that appear in holographic models. The second case is when the deformation is perturbatively integrable to some order in the deformation parameter but can not be extended to an integrable model. In this paper we work this out for the XXZ spin chain and discuss the level statistics of each of these cases. We find numerical evidence that the onset of chaos occurs differently in each of these models. For the perturbatively integrable models, we find that the deformation strength at which chaos appears demonstrates a volume-scaling intermediate between strong and weak integrability breaking models.
item.dc:creator: Ysla F. Adans, Marius de Leeuw, Tristan McLoughlin

item.title: Poisson bracket and $L_\infty$ algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.30630v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the Poisson bracket of a Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. If the symplectic structure on phase space is defined following recent work, we show that the Poisson bracket can be computed with the Peierls formula, confirming the well-known result of the covariant phase space formalism. Of particular interest is the Poisson bracket in nonlocal theories. In $p$-adic string theory we find that a straightforward construction of the Poisson bracket is obstructed by higher derivative instabilities. We also discuss the inverse relation between the Poisson bracket and symplectic structure in the language of homological algebra, extending some ideas in the mathematical physics literature.
item.dc:creator: Vin\'icius Bernardes, Theodore Erler, Atakan Hilmi F{\i}rat, Igor Khavkine

item.title: Quantum-classical crossover in finite spin-1/2 rings with Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction
item.description: arXiv:2607.13572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study finite spin-$\tfrac12$ rings with nearest-neighbor Heisenberg exchange, Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction, and an external magnetic field. We introduce a phenomenological interpolation parameter between the fully quantum Hamiltonian and a state-dependent mean-field description. Using dissipative Gisin-Schr\"odinger dynamics, we analyze the resulting quantum-classical crossover through local magnetization, connected spin correlations, single-site entropy, and the saturation field of the fully polarized state.
item.dc:creator: Ra\'ul S\'anchez Gal\'an, Robert Wieser

item.title: Entangled measurements are necessary for optimal tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states and of bosonic Gaussian states near the vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2609.23189v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that learning an unknown mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes to trace distance $\epsilon$ requires $\Omega(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies when measurements act on one copy at a time, even with arbitrary POVMs, fresh ancillas and classical adaptivity, but without quantum memory between copies. The bound holds for $0<\epsilon\le1/3600$ and separates this model from the known collective rate $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. It follows from a uniform single-copy Fisher-information budget and a dimension-independent comparison between trace distance and Gaussian parameters. On covariance matrices of operator norm at most $1-c$, we prove a Frobenius-to-trace-norm continuity bound with constant $[2c(2-c)]^{-1/2}$; matchgate shadows then attain $O(m^3/(c\epsilon^2))$ copies. This also gives explicit error certificates for thermal free-fermion states. For a class of mixed passive bosonic Gaussian states with total mean photon number at most one, a reduction to bounded-block qudit tomography gives a single-copy lower bound $\Omega(m^3/(\epsilon^2\sqrt{\log(m/\epsilon)}))$, versus collective complexity $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. These separations answer the mixed-state measurement-resource question posed by Chen et al. A two-mode example has optimal two-copy Fisher trace $5$, versus the separable ceiling $4$. An IBM replication gave a pre-registered witness lower bound $4.12$ at one-sided $95\%$ shot-noise confidence; its interpretation assumes the prescribed preparations and a common measurement channel and does not bound preparation systematics.
item.dc:creator: Ron Rubin (Rubin Anders Scientific, Inc.)

item.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
item.description: arXiv:2609.40068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emie Szeftel

item.title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
item.description: arXiv:2609.40315v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emie Szeftel

item.title: Strict non-tightness of the level-3 quantum bootstrap for a coupled three-dimensional double well, at an excited eigenstate
item.description: arXiv:2610.03362v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the coupled three-dimensional double well $H=\tfrac12|p|^2+2\sum_i(q_i^2-1)^2-\sum_{i<j}q_i^2q_j^2$ we exhibit, at the first excited energy level (and also at the ground state), a linear functional on polynomials of degree $\le 6$ that satisfies every constraint of the standard level-3 eigenstate bootstrap, has a strictly positive definite moment matrix, and nevertheless assigns a negative value to a nonnegative polynomial. It is therefore an interior point of the level-3 relaxation that is realized by no quantum state. The construction reflects a fact that holds at every level: the eigenstate rows never reach the top-degree momentum moments. At level 3, where strictly feasible points exist, this means that the corresponding block of the moment matrix carries no information about which energies admit one. Every algebraic ingredient is an exact rational certificate, and the only numerical ingredients (spectral enclosures of an eigenfunction) are carried out in rigorous ball arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Keren, Ye Zhou

item.title: Seifert type magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.08519v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains whose magnetic lines define an $(m,n)$ Seifert fibration for arbitrary coprime integers $m,n$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Peralta-Salas, Radu Slobodeanu

item.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.34240v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a Wilsonian framework, globally controlled across the holonomy space, for determining the perturbative data governing the vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on a circle. This allows lifting the Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua in 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Chern--Simons-matter theories to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. The framework is showcased by finding a rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple U(1) model and by reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction (first diagnosed on $S^3\times S^1$) of an SU(2) Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory.
item.dc:creator: Arash Arabi Ardehali

item.title: Haagerup vertex operator algebras at central charge eight
item.description:
arXiv:2611.01618v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evans and Gannon showed that a positive vertex operator algebra of central charge eight whose representation category is the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category has one of two character vectors, with six or nineteen currents. Call such an algebra, if strongly rational, a Haagerup algebra. We prove that a Haagerup algebra $U$ has six currents, that $U_1 \cong \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2$ embeds into $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ in one of two explicit ways, with levels $(1,39)$ or $(3,13)$, and we determine the lowest weight spaces of its modules and $U_2$ as $U_1$-modules. For the levels $(3,13)$, $U_2$ is one of four Galois conjugate subspaces. Together with $U_1$ it generates the unitary $C_2$-cofinite algebra $S$, which is isomorphic to the algebra constructed by Jiao. For the levels $(1,39)$, $U$ contains the explicit algebra of Riesen. The associated lattice of $U$ is that of the form $x^2+xy+10y^2$, resp.\ $3x^2+3xy+4y^2$, the two classes of the principal genus of discriminant $-39$. Exchanging them in the decomposition of $U$ over its Heisenberg commutant gives a Haagerup algebra $U^
atural$ of the other levels, and $U \mapsto U^
atural$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of the two cases. The classification gives exactly two isomorphism classes, forming a single hyperbolic genus, as soon as either explicit candidate is known to be a Haagerup algebra. This property is proved for $S$ in [ArhIII], where the twin $S^
atural$ is also identified, with the algebra of Huang and Riesen, using the results of Dong, Jiao and Xu [DJX26]. The explicit algebras of Jiao and Riesen have rational forms. The proofs combine exact trace relations given by vector-valued modular forms, exact computations in a model of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, and genera of vertex operator algebras.
item.dc:creator: C\'edric Arhancet

item.title: A hierarchy of physics-embedded neural operators for structural dynamic surrogate modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.07059v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Structural-response surrogates must capture moving resonances, phase changes, and unequal-amplitude transfer channels during optimization or health-state changes. Physics-embedded learning seeks FEA-level accuracy at lower cost by embedding physics in inputs, forward passes, losses, and backpropagation. We propose Modal Rational (MR), mapping structural features to modal quantities for analytical frequency-response reconstruction. The Physics-Guided Modal Operator Network (PGMON) adds bounded frequency, damping, and residual-flexibility corrections. Modal Operator with Structural GELU and Anchored-SIREN Correction (MOSAIC) denotes the bounded spectral-discrepancy framework used here; MOSAIC-MR and MOSAIC-PGMON add such discrepancies. They support finite-dimensional maps and physical decoders for future neural operators; evidence is fixed-topology, not a completed operator comparison. Two 20,000-design populations are studied: an 80 m steel truss tower with variable member areas and attached masses, and a tapered shell beam with ten variable station masses. Archived tests cover ten designs and seven acceleration histories per structure; they are benchmarks, not seismic-design assessments. With 5% reference modal damping, MR, PGMON, and MOSAIC give mean displacement-history errors of 0.73-0.76% for the tower and 0.029-0.116% for the beam, against declared band-limited modal references. Supplied modal frequencies are distinguished from design-only use; unequal parameter counts and training settings are explicit. Error analysis separates learned modal discrepancies, truncation, and excitation weighting, explaining acceleration and difficult-tower limits and risks of blind use. Results support physically structured prediction but limit claims about generalization, computational savings, and added corrections. Next is developing and validating neural operators around these architectures.
item.dc:creator: Amir Nasrollahi, Mehmet Sefa Orak

item.title: Dualities in one-dimensional quantum lattice models: Lie groups, Schur-Weyl duality and symmetry breaking
item.description: arXiv:2611.08293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic framework for gauging continuous symmetries, and show that the Schur-Weyl duality arises naturally as a realization of this construction with open boundary conditions. Restricting to compact Lie group symmetries, we construct dual models for one-dimensional quantum lattice models exhibiting those symmetries. We demonstrate that matrix product operators enable the explicit construction of intertwiners between the dual theories and their (non-invertible) symmetries. With closed boundary conditions, we can relate the full spectrum of these dual theories by considering all possible twisted boundary conditions. We illustrate how the Peter-Weyl transform appears when the duality acts on the boundary Hilbert space of a $G$-symmetric model. The presented framework generalizes previous work on dualities for unitary fusion category symmetric models. It exemplifies how dualities for both finite and continuous symmetries rely on the relation between a bond algebra and a representation of the symmetry in the lattice as double centralizers. We argue that dual non-invertible spontaneous symmetry breaking is the mechanism that underlies symmetric tensor network algorithms. We illustrate these results for $U(1)$- and $SU(2)$-symmetric quantum lattice models.
item.dc:creator: Dante Bosgoed, Frank Verstraete, Laurens Lootens
